subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should repeated exec calls with identical nonzero structured outcomes count as no progress even when their stdout or stderr changes meaningfully?
rationale: Tests prove the proposed behavior, but they cannot decide the product tradeoff between stopping runaway retries and avoiding false-positive blocking of legitimate nonzero polling workflows.

options.title: Accept stable nonzero fingerprints
options.body: Refresh the branch, resolve the two failing checks, and land the documented behavior because bounded runaway-loop prevention outweighs rare long-running nonzero polling cases.

options.title: Preserve semantic failure output
options.body: Revise completed nonzero hashing to retain a normalized semantic output summary, reducing false positives at the cost of more complex and potentially brittle volatility filtering.
